summary: Miriam Levering was a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. She earned her PhD from Harvard University in 1978 and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tennessee (attested 2007–2010).

Mirjan Damaška studied at Zagreb, the Hague Academy, the International Faculty of Comparative Law, and Ljubljana (PhD 1960). He taught at Zagreb, the International Faculty of Comparative Law, Pennsylvania, and Yale, serving at Yale Law School from around 1976 to 2000.
Mitchell G. Weiss is an Indologist who studied under Ludo Rocher. He has held a post as professor at the University of Basel.
Mithilesh Chaturvedi is a scholar of Indology and linguistics affiliated with the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Delhi, where he was attested in 2009 and as professor emeritus in 2026.

Mitsuji Fukunaga was a philosopher and Sinologist educated at Hiroshima Higher Normal School and Kyoto University. He taught at Kitano High School, Aichi University of Education, Kyoto University (1961–1982), University of Tokyo (1974–1979), Kansai University, and University of Kitakyushu.

Mitsukuni Yoshida was a scholar of Japanology and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1942 to 1945 and later held a post at Kyoto University of the Arts from around 1989 to 1991.
Mitsunobu Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a part-time lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 2005) and held a post at Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (attested 2020).
Mitsutoshi Moriguchi is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he later served as a lecturer (attested 1989–1995).
Mitsuyo Demoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University and held a post at the University of Marburg (attested 2024).

Mitsuyoshi Saegusa was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Tokyo, Munich (PhD), and Kokugakuin (doctorate), and held academic posts at Kokugakuin, Nihon University, the University of Tsukuba (1975–1987), and Toho Gakuin.

Mitsuyuki Ishida was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He served as a professor at Ryukoku University from around 1950 to 1974 and later as a professor at Shitennoji University (attested 1976).
Miyako Notake is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who has served as a part-time lecturer at Waseda University (attested 2015 and 2026).

Mizuho Okita is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Tokai and Gakushuin universities under Katsuhiko Kamimura and Atsuhiko Yoshida. She served as a part-time lecturer at Meisei University around 2008.
Mizumaro Ishida was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who served as a professor at Tokai University (attested 1976 and 1987).
Mohammad Ashraf Dar is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who completed a Master of Philosophy at Vikram University, where he was also attested as a research scholar in 2014.

Mohammad Habib was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at the University of Allahabad (ca. 1911–1916), Aligarh Muslim University, and New College (ca. 1916–1919).

Mokurai Shimaji was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Chō Sanshū. He held leadership posts at Nishi Hongan-ji and Hongan-ji, served as the 25th chief priest at Gankyo-ji (1892–1905), and founded Chiyoda Jogakuen.

Mona Schrempf is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned a doctorate in anthropology from the Free University of Berlin (2001) and held posts at the Humboldt University of Berlin and Heidelberg University (both attested 2006).

Monica Esposito was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. She studied at Venice, Fudan, Ghent, Shanghai, and Paris (PhD 1993), and later served as an associate professor at Kyoto University from around 2003 to 2011.

Monica L. Smith is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied at the University of Michigan (ca. 1991–1997). She held a post at the University of Pittsburgh (2000–2002) before joining the University of California, Los Angeles in 2002.
